questions.prompt: In the greedy activity-selection algorithm, activities are sorted by...
questions.explanation: Choosing the activity that finishes earliest leaves the most room for the rest — the greedy choice that is provably optimal here.

questions.prompt: Which property must hold for a greedy algorithm to yield a globally optimal solution?

options.text: A sorted input in all cases

questions.explanation: The greedy-choice property says a globally optimal solution is reachable by making locally optimal choices; it must be proved for each problem.

questions.prompt: Which statements about greedy algorithms are true? Select all that apply.

options.text: They make a locally optimal choice at each step and don't backtrack
Activity selection by finish time is optimal
Huffman coding is a greedy algorithm
Greedy by value/weight ratio solves 0/1 knapsack optimally

questions.explanation: Greedy commits to local optima; activity selection and Huffman are optimal greedy algorithms. Greedy is NOT optimal for 0/1 knapsack — that needs DP.

questions.prompt: A greedy algorithm makes the ______ optimal choice at each step. (one word)
questions.explanation: It optimizes the immediate choice, trusting (when the greedy-choice property holds) that this leads to a global optimum.

questions.prompt: Order the steps of the greedy activity-selection algorithm.

items.text: Skip activities that overlap the last chosen one
Select the next compatible activity, and repeat

questions.explanation: Sort by finish, take the earliest-finishing activity, then repeatedly take the next one that starts after the last chosen finishes.

questions.prompt: Match each problem with its greedy fact.
questions.explanation: Three of these are solved optimally by greedy; 0/1 knapsack is the classic case where greedy fails and dynamic programming is required.
